title: Financial Investigation: Purpose and Principles
summary: Why every profit-generating crime should have a financial dimension, the objectives a financial investigation can serve, and what the FATF standards expect of investigative authorities.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Why every profit-generating crime should have a financial dimension, the objectives a financial investigation can serve, and what the FATF standards expect of investigative authorities.
Learning Objectives: Explain the evidential, intelligence and asset recovery purposes of financial investigation
Distinguish parallel financial investigations from stand-alone money laundering cases
Summarise the FATF expectations for investigative powers and outcomes
Syllabus: Following the money: proving offences, finding assets and mapping networks
Parallel financial investigation alongside predicate offence cases
FATF Recommendations 30 and 31 and Immediate Outcome 7
The financial investigator's role in a multi-disciplinary team
Intended Audience: Police and agency investigators handling acquisitive, organised or economic crime
Financial investigators, intelligence analysts and FIU staff supporting investigations
Asset recovery, customs and tax investigators who trace and evidence criminal finances
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of criminal investigation, intelligence analysis or financial crime work is helpful. No accounting qualification is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2012), Operational Issues: Financial Investigations Guidance
FATF (2012, as updated), International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations
FATF and Egmont Group (2018), Concealment of Beneficial Ownership
FATF (2023), Guidance on Beneficial Ownership for Legal Persons
